Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2) — a from-scratch visual/UX redesign ("Nexion") of a hosting platform's customer dashboard, built on a real backend. This is a READ-ONLY audit before production promotion — do not edit or fix anything, only report findings with file:line evidence.

Part 1 — Activity Log. The `ActivityLog` Prisma model recently gained NEW fields as part of this redesign: `ip` (caller's IP, null for system actions), `category` (server|billing|security|team|files|database|schedule|other, derived at write time), `orgId` (for the Team screen's activity log), `target` (what the action was performed ON, e.g. "Palworld Server"). Audit app/dashboard/activity (find exact path) and its backing action/query code:
1. Are these four new fields actually POPULATED when activity log rows are written? Search for where `db.activityLog.create` (or similar) is called across the codebase and check whether `ip`/`category`/`orgId`/`target` are actually set, or left null everywhere (meaning the schema fields exist but nothing writes them, making the "category filter" and "IP address column" and Team activity log permanently empty/non-functional).
2. Does the Activity page's UI actually filter/display by `category`, show the `ip` column, and does the Team screen show org-scoped activity via `orgId`? Or does the UI expect these but get null forever?

Part 2 — Notifications. Search for NotificationsPanel (components/nx/Banners.tsx or similar) and lib/prefs.ts (mentioned in a schema comment as owning notification-preference policy separate from UserPreference).
3. Are real notifications actually created and delivered (in-app + email) for real events (payment failure, service suspension, 2FA change, etc.), or is the notifications UI showing static/empty content?
4. Does `lib/prefs.ts`'s policy of "some notifications cannot be suppressed" actually get enforced in the send path, or is this aspirational/comment-only?

Part 3 — Support tickets. Find the support ticket area (app/dashboard/support or similar).
5. Is ticket creation, reply, and attachment upload real (Prisma-backed, real file storage/validation), and do admin-side replies show up for the customer? Quick check only — this feature had a lightbox bug fixed earlier this session (unrelated, don't re-check that), just confirm no NEW backend gaps in ticket creation/reply/attachments.

Report as a table: Feature | REAL / PARTIAL / STUB / NEVER WRITTEN | evidence (file:line) | what's missing. Keep under 700 words total across all 3 parts. Do not modify any files.

# Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # read-only query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server. Treat it as read-only.** Never write to the prod DB (the `db` subcommand refuses obvious writes, which is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary), never edit `/opt/nxeon`, never build there, never restart a prod service. If you genuinely need to change something on node-1, **stop and ask the owner first.** ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run builds in `/opt/nxeon`.** That is live production; clobbering its `.next` has taken the admin panel down before. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. ## Verification discipline A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**. There is a login-and-capture script: ```bash node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS ``` Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. Read the PNG back and actually look at it — a sliced game wordmark, a clipped top bar and an empty Mods tab were all invisible in the code and obvious in a screenshot. ## Things that have already cost hours here - **Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls.** Always `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && …`. - **`git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks.** Write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`. - **`git bundle create f A..B` with two raw SHAs** makes a bundle with no refs, which git refuses as empty. The tip must be a named ref: `A..design/v2`. - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` aurora layer paints above static content.** Page content needs `relative z-[1]`. - **A `backdrop-filter` ancestor becomes the containing block for `fixed` children** — `createPortal` to `document.body` instead. - **Never size a fixed overlay from a header's height.** That is the header's bottom edge only when nothing sits above it, and the sandbox banner does. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - **Do not** run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

16	 * reports success and is read by nothing — the auto-suspend kill switch an
17	 * operator turned off before watching customer VMs get suspended anyway
18	 * (P1-5), and the domain-markup panel that displayed 0% while charging 25%
19	 * (P1-9).
20	 *
21	 * The dangerous half of fixing it is OVER-fixing it. If a preference could
22	 * suppress a declined payment, an imminent suspension, a security/2FA change or
23	 * a data-loss warning, then an unticked checkbox would silently swallow the one
24	 * message the customer had to see — and they would lose a server, or an
25	 * account, with no warning at all. That is strictly worse than the original bug.
26	 *
27	 * So suppressibility is decided by a message's TIER, declared once in the
28	 * catalogue below, and never by the call site. A send site cannot make itself
29	 * suppressible by passing the wrong flag, and an unrecognised kind resolves to
30	 * CRITICAL — if we guess wrong, we guess towards "delivered".
31	 */
32	
33	export type NotificationPrefs = {
34	  /**
35	   * Non-urgent transactional EMAIL: payment receipts, activity notices.
36	   * Never covers the dunning sequence, suspensions or security changes.
37	   */
38	  email: boolean;
39	  /**
40	   * Product news / marketing. Unticking this also removes the address from the
41	   * campaign list (see `updateNotificationPrefs`) — the stored flag alone would
42	   * suppress nothing, because campaigns are addressed by email, not by user.
43	   */
44	  product: boolean;
45	  /**
46	   * Legacy key, pinned `true`.
47	   *
48	   * It used to render as a "Security alerts" toggle, which was dishonest twice
49	   * over: the channel it claimed to govern was never built (sign-in / token /
50	   * 2FA paths write audit rows only), and security, password and 2FA messages
51	   * must not be suppressible in the first place. Kept in the shape so
52	   * previously-stored values and the GDPR export keep round-tripping, and typed
53	   * as the literal `true` so no code path can ever write it back as
54	   * consent-withdrawn.
55	   */
56	  security: true;
57	};
58	
59	export const DEFAULT_PREFS: NotificationPrefs = { email: true, product: true, security: true };
60	
61	/**
62	 * Normalise whatever is stored in the Json column into a typed prefs object.
63	 * A missing or malformed key falls back to the default (opted IN) — the column
64	 * is nullable and predates this policy, so "absent" must never read as "the
65	 * customer opted out of everything".
66	 */
67	export function normalizePrefs(raw: unknown): NotificationPrefs {
68	  const p = (raw ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
69	  return {
70	    email: typeof p.email === "boolean" ? p.email : DEFAULT_PREFS.email,
71	    product: typeof p.product === "boolean" ? p.product : DEFAULT_PREFS.product,
72	    security: true,
73	  };
74	}
75	
76	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
77	/*                          Delivery policy                                   */
78	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
79	
80	/** How a message reaches the customer. */
81	export type NotifyChannel = "email" | "inapp";
82	
83	/**
84	 * Suppressibility tier.
85	 *
86	 * CRITICAL — "you need to know this". Delivered on every channel, always,
87	 *            whatever the preferences say. Money that failed to move, a service
88	 *            about to be suspended or deleted, a change to how the account is
89	 *            secured, or anything that can cost the customer data.
90	 * ACCOUNT  — informational transactional. Email is suppressible via
91	 *            `prefs.email`; the in-app bell is kept (see `isSuppressible`).
92	 * PRODUCT  — marketing. Suppressible on every channel via `prefs.product`.
93	 */
94	export type NotifyTier = "CRITICAL" | "ACCOUNT" | "PRODUCT";
95	
96	/**
97	 * Every message kind the platform can send, and the ONE thing that decides
98	 * whether a preference may hold it back. Grouped by tier so the split is
99	 * reviewable at a glance — adding a kind is a deliberate act, and putting
100	 * something in ACCOUNT is a statement that a customer missing it entirely costs
101	 * them nothing they cannot recover.
102	 */
103	export const NOTIFY_KINDS = {
104	  // ---- CRITICAL: never suppressible, on any channel, by any preference. -----
105	  /** Password-reset link. The only way back into a locked-out account. */
106	  password_reset: "CRITICAL",
107	  /**
108	   * Email-verification link. CRITICAL for the same reason as the reset link, not
109	   * because it is urgent: an unverified account cannot buy or provision
110	   * (lib/email-verification.ts), so this message is the ONLY way past that gate.
111	   * Letting a preference suppress it would leave the customer refused at
112	   * checkout with no way to fix it — a locked door whose key we withheld.
113	   */
114	  email_verify: "CRITICAL",
115	  /** Password changed, 2FA enabled/disabled, backup codes reissued, API token created/revoked. */
116	  security_change: "CRITICAL",
117	  /** Card declined, dunning retry declined, final notice. Money did not move. */
118	  payment_failed: "CRITICAL",
119	  /** 3-D Secure / `requires_action` — the payment stalls until the customer acts. */
120	  payment_action_required: "CRITICAL",
121	  /** Saved card expires soon: the next renewal will fail if it is not replaced. */
122	  card_expiring: "CRITICAL",
123	  /** Term is about to lapse. Suppressing this is how a paid-up customer loses a VM. */
124	  expiry_warning: "CRITICAL",
125	  /** Service suspended, or about to be. */
126	  suspension: "CRITICAL",
127	  /** Service terminated, or about to be — data destruction is imminent/done. */
128	  termination: "CRITICAL",
129	  /** Abuse / acceptable-use action against the account. */
130	  abuse: "CRITICAL",
131	  /** Anything that lost, or may lose, customer data (failed backup, restore, volume). */
132	  data_loss: "CRITICAL",
133	  /** Paid but not provisioned — the customer's money is in limbo. */
134	  fulfilment_failed: "CRITICAL",
135	  /**
136	   * Server provisioned and reachable — the deployment confirmation carrying the
137	   * customer's SSH connection details. The positive resolution of the same
138	   * money-path as `fulfilment_failed`, and CRITICAL for the same reason: it must
139	   * ALWAYS send. A stranded customer whose status was silently wrong (see the
140	   * reconcile recovery) may never have received it, so suppressing it by a
141	   * preference would leave someone who paid for a server unable to find the door.
142	   */
143	  provision_ready: "CRITICAL",
144	  /** Refund or write-off issued against the account. */
145	  refund: "CRITICAL",
146	
147	  // ---- ACCOUNT: informational transactional. Email opt-out honoured. -------
148	  welcome: "ACCOUNT",
149	  /** Receipt for a payment that SUCCEEDED. (A failure is `payment_failed`.) */
150	  receipt: "ACCOUNT",
151	  invoice: "ACCOUNT",
152	  /** Deploy / reinstall / migration finished successfully. */
153	  provision_done: "ACCOUNT",
154	  /** Backup taken, app installed, certificate issued, volume attached, … */
155	  job_done: "ACCOUNT",
156	  /** Domain registered / renewed / transferred. */
157	  domain_activity: "ACCOUNT",
158	  support_reply: "ACCOUNT",
159	  referral_bonus: "ACCOUNT",
160	
161	  // ---- PRODUCT: marketing. Suppressible everywhere. ------------------------
162	  product_news: "PRODUCT",
163	} as const satisfies Record<string, NotifyTier>;
164	
165	export type NotifyKind = keyof typeof NOTIFY_KINDS;
166	
167	/**
168	 * Tier of a message kind. An unregistered kind resolves to CRITICAL on purpose:
169	 * the failure mode of a mis-typed or forgotten kind must be "delivered anyway",
170	 * never "silently dropped".
171	 */
172	export function notifyTier(kind: NotifyKind): NotifyTier {
173	  return (NOTIFY_KINDS as Record<string, NotifyTier>)[kind] ?? "CRITICAL";
174	}
175	
176	/**
177	 * Does this (kind, channel) pair depend on the customer's preferences at all?
178	 *
179	 * `false` means the answer is unconditionally "deliver", so callers can skip the
180	 * preference lookup entirely — the gate costs nothing on the critical paths.
181	 */
182	export function isSuppressible(kind: NotifyKind, channel: NotifyChannel): boolean {
183	  const tier = notifyTier(kind);
184	  if (tier === "CRITICAL") return false;
185	  if (tier === "ACCOUNT") {
186	    // Email only. The in-app bell is the durable record inside the portal, and
187	    // the toggle the customer ticked says "email" — hiding an activity notice
188	    // from the portal would recreate the very failure this policy exists to
189	    // cure (information that quietly went missing), while suppressing the mail
190	    // is exactly what was asked for.
191	    return channel === "email";
192	  }
193	  return true; // PRODUCT — marketing has no business on a channel they declined.
194	}
195	
196	/** Decide delivery from already-loaded preferences. */
197	export function mayDeliver(
198	  prefs: NotificationPrefs,
199	  kind: NotifyKind,
200	  channel: NotifyChannel,
201	): boolean {
202	  if (!isSuppressible(kind, channel)) return true;
203	  return notifyTier(kind) === "PRODUCT" ? prefs.product : prefs.email;
204	}
205	
206	/**
207	 * Decide delivery for a user id, loading their preferences only when the answer
208	 * actually depends on them.
209	 *
210	 * Fails OPEN. A missing user row or a database hiccup returns `true`: a message
211	 * must never be dropped because a preference lookup failed — that would be a
212	 * silent swallow with no preference behind it at all.
213	 *
214	 * `./db` is imported lazily so this module stays statically safe to import from
215	 * anywhere (the settings page imports `normalizePrefs`, the client component
216	 * imports the type only).
217	 */
218	export async function mayDeliverTo(
219	  userId: string,
220	  kind: NotifyKind,
221	  channel: NotifyChannel,
222	): Promise<boolean> {
223	  if (!isSuppressible(kind, channel)) return true;
224	  try {
225	    const { db } = await import("./db");
226	    const row = await db.user.findUnique({
227	      where: { id: userId },
228	      select: { notificationPrefs: true },
229	    });
230	    if (!row) return true;
231	    return mayDeliver(normalizePrefs(row.notificationPrefs), kind, channel);
232	  } catch {
233	    return true;
234	  }
235	}

## Audit Report

| # | Feature | Status | Evidence | What's missing |
|---|---------|--------|----------|-----------------|
| 1 | AuditLog new fields (`ip`, `category`, `orgId`, `target`) populated at write time | **NEVER WRITTEN** | Every `db.auditLog.create`/`.createMany` call across `lib/actions-*.ts`, `worker/*.ts`, and the shared writer `lib/audit.ts:21` (`recordAudit`) only sets `{ userId, action, detail }`. Searched all ~200+ call sites (grep for `ip:`/`category:`/`orgId:`/`target:` within 500 chars of an `auditLog.create(` call) — zero hits; the few `ip:`/`target:` string matches nearby were unrelated code (`server.ts:1151` local var, `target.userId` variable). Field doc comments exist only in `prisma/schema.prisma:950-964`. | Nobody sets these columns; they are permanently `null` for every row ever written. |
| 2 | Activity page: category filter, IP column, Team org-scoped log | **PARTIAL / STUB (self-aware)** | `app/dashboard/activity/page.tsx:50` falls back to a derived `categoryOf(action)` (`lib/nx/activity.ts`) when `r.category` is null — so category filtering works via derivation, not the stored column, which is fine since it's always null anyway. `ip` is read (`page.tsx:53`, `r.ip ?? ""`) but always renders empty since it's never written — an "IP address" column that is permanently blank. `app/dashboard/team/page.tsx:46-53` explicitly does NOT use `orgId`; its own comment says "AuditLog rows carry the ACTOR's userId, not an orgId... not a feed of everything everyone in the org did" — it queries `where: { userId: user.id, action: {startsWith:"org."} }` instead. So the Team activity feature is honestly scoped down to work around the unused `orgId` field rather than being broken silently. |
| 3 | Notifications: real events → in-app + email | **REAL** | `db.notification.create/.createMany` fires from real event sites: `worker/billing.ts` (payment failed/suspension, many sites), `lib/actions-payment-method.ts:90`, `lib/actions-2fa.ts` writes audit only but security_change routes through `lib/mailer.ts:242` → `mayDeliverTo`; ticket replies via `lib/reply-core.ts:90-207`, `lib/ticket-reply-email.ts:114`. Email delivery goes through `lib/mailer.ts:242` (`mayDeliverTo(opts.userId, opts.kind, "email")`). |
| 4 | `lib/prefs.ts` "some notifications can't be suppressed" enforced in send path | **REAL** | `lib/prefs.ts:182-194` (`isSuppressible`) returns `false` for any `CRITICAL` tier kind (payment_failed, suspension, security_change, etc., listed lines 104-146), enforced centrally in `lib/mailer.ts:242` (the shared `sendMail`), plus explicit call sites: `lib/actions-account.ts:210,259` (password_reset), `lib/payment-failed-recovery.ts:59-61`, `worker/dormant-winback.ts:127`, `worker/deploy-winback.ts:182-184`. Fails open on DB error (`lib/prefs.ts:230-234`) by design, never silently drops critical mail. |
| 5 | Support tickets: creation/reply/attachments real backend, admin replies visible to customer | **REAL** | `lib/actions-support.ts:55-79` (`createTicket`, Zod-validated, Prisma-backed via `createTicketCore`), `:86-` (`replyTicket`, ownership double-checked, `lib/reply-core.ts`), `lib/ticket-attachment.ts:100-156` (magic-byte signature validation for images/PDF/ZIP/text, 10MB cap, SVG blocked, declared-MIME never trusted). `TicketMessage.isStaff`/`readAt` (`prisma/schema.prisma:395-411`) drive staff-reply visibility and read receipts to the customer. No new backend gaps found in this quick pass (lightbox bug excluded as instructed). |

**Bottom line:** Part 1 is the real defect — the schema fields (`ip`, `category`, `orgId`, `target`) are 100% decorative; nothing populates them. The Activity page compensates for `category` via a derive-on-read fallback and for `orgId` by intentionally scoping the Team feed to `userId` instead (with an honest code comment). The `ip` column is the one genuinely dead UI element — it will render blank forever until some auth/action-layer code captures the request IP and passes it into `auditLog.create`. Parts 2–3 (notifications/prefs, support tickets) are real, Prisma-backed, and functioning as designed.
